raw_response:
I farm the same land my father farmed. In Quzhou, everyone plants wheat in the autumn and maize after the wheat comes off in June. That's how it's always been. The soil here is flat and deep, good for both. I don't know much about new techniques — I learned by working beside my father since I was a boy, and I watch what my neighbors do.

I have about 8 mu. All of it goes into wheat first, then maize on the same ground. No point trying something different — cotton prices are bad and I don't know how to grow vegetables for market.

For wheat seed, I'll go to the supply shop in town and buy the improved variety they're pushing this year. Same for maize — hybrid seeds, that's what everyone uses now. My cousin tried saving his own maize seeds once, the yield was terrible.

Fertilizer: I'll spread compound fertilizer before plowing, then add urea when the wheat is jointing and again at heading. For maize I'll put down more urea when it's knee-high. My neighbor uses a lot of urea and his fields look good, so I follow what he does.

Wheat needs water badly — I'll pump from the well at least three times. Maize grows in the rainy season so usually once is enough unless it's a dry summer.

I'll plow deep before wheat so the roots go down. Before maize I'll just rotary till after combining — faster and the soil is already loose.
